meeting_header: Date: 2026-12-21 | Start: 16:00 PST | Duration: 62m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Lucas (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Aisha (Head of ML, Graymatter), Tom (Infra Lead), Sarah (Finance), Kevin (Product)
summary: Quarterly operational and fiscal alignment focused on managing recent usage spike, evaluating Dedicated vs Hosted for predictable latencies, and lining up a January pilot. Action items: pricing sheet, perf benchmark, and security docs to unblock procurement.
topics: dedicated capacity and private deployment considerations
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Okay everyone, thanks for joining. This is Maya from Redwood, Lucas is our SE, Priya from CSM as well. Confirming we have Aisha, Tom, Sarah, Kevin from Graymatter. Yup?
[00:18] Aisha: Yeah hi, thanks. Quick reminder we are on a hard deadline—finance wants clarity before end of year for the Q1 pilot commitment.
[00:25] Maya: Absolutely, that's why today we'll walk through the usage trends, cost options, and the reliability tradeoffs, and then nail down next steps.
[00:32] Tom: Real quick, we saw a 3x spike over last two weeks—mostly inference for routing and ETA updates. That drove token spend way up and some 95th percentile latency blips during peaks.
[00:45] Lucas: When you say blips, do you mean queueing at the loader or tail latency from model?
[00:51] Tom: More queueing. Our load tests show batch buildup, but also some KV cache misses. Might be cache warmup.
[01:05] Maya: That aligns with what we saw in telemetry. We flagged a few routes with long seq lengths—model selection and seq length distribution matter a lot here.
[01:12] Sarah: From finance side we need to see delta between hosted per-token costs vs a reserved Dedicated pool. We want predictability—no surprise invoices.
[01:21] Maya: Totally. We prepared a committed pricing scenario and a high-level cost model for Dedicated vs hosted with burst economics. I'll share the spreadsheet.
[01:29] Lucas: Technical note: Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and isolated GPUs; you can pin model variants and use aggressive batching. Hosted gives simpler ops but the unit-cost can be higher under sustained heavy usage.
[01:41] Aisha: For accuracy, we can't lose the reranker quality. Any quantization path that materially changes output is a non-starter.
[01:49] Lucas: Understood. We recommend 8-bit quant profiles for the cheaper path but hold the reranker on FP16 for the critical flows—this hybrid profile often keeps quality within tolerance while dropping cost ~30%.
[02:02] Tom: Can you remind me about KV cache behavior across Dedicated nodes? We had some mismatch earlier; cache was invalidated during autoscale.
[02:12] Lucas: That's a good callout. Our runtime maintains per-instance KV cache; autoscaling requires careful sticky routing or shared prefix cache. We can configure sticky affinity for those heavy routes to avoid warmup, or enable global prefix caching in the private deployment. There's a slight tradeoff with scheduling efficiency.
[02:30] Speaker 1: (inaudible) kv cash, sorry.
[02:34] Maya: No worries. On security, Sarah, you wanted SOC2 and KMS?
[02:39] Sarah: Yep, procurement wants SOC2 Type II and proof of key management controls; also vendor access matrix and SSO integration details.
[02:47] Maya: We'll attach SOC2 docs, and a KMS integration note. For private deployment we support customer KMS/HSM and SAML-based SSO; for hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS options.
[03:02] Aisha: Network wise we need a VPC peering option and egress audit logs for GDPR needs. Any problem with that?
[03:10] Lucas: We support VPC peering and customer-managed subnets for Private. For hosted we do region isolation and can provide audit logs; there may be additional retentions charges for long-term log storage.
[03:22] Kevin: Are there restrictions on model rollout? We need canary testing and quick rollback paths—especially during releases.
[03:29] Lucas: Yes, our console supports A/B and canary rollouts per-route with automatic fallback policies. You can pin versions and define SLA-based fallback thresholds.
[03:40] Tom: On perf, if we go dedicated, what kind of SLOs are realistic for 95th percentile at 2k concurrent sessions?
[03:49] Lucas: With Dedicated and proper batching, you should expect sub-200ms 95th for our causal LLMs at 2k concurrent moderate-length requests; longer sequences will push that up. We'll validate with your seq distribution.
[04:05] Aisha: We also run reranker at high qps; that path is sensitive because it's out-of-band and can't batch as effectively.
[04:12] Lucas: For rerankers we recommend a separate smaller dedicated pool with low-latency nodes or keep it on FP16 and smaller context windows. Also we can tune batching window to keep tail low.
[04:25] Maya: I'm going to share a small matrix of configuration levers: batching/window, sticky routing, quantization profile, and dedicated pool sizing—this'll map to estimated cost per 1M tokens.
[04:35] Sarah: We need that mapped to monthly committed spend ranges so procurement can pick a tier.
[04:41] Maya: Absolutely. I'll send committed tiers with ramp schedules.
[04:45] Aisha: One risk: residency. We process some EU data—do you support data residency controls?
[04:52] Lucas: Yes—region pinning for data egress, and Private with on-prem can fully isolate. For hosted we have EU regions with restricted egress and key separation.
[05:04] Tom: Something we hit in the spike: autoscale delays during cold start created a 30–45s window where 99th spiked. Is there a warm standby option?
[05:15] Lucas: We offer burst capacity and warm pools in Dedicated; you can reserve headroom to avoid cold starts. There's a cost tradeoff but it's controllable.
[05:25] Maya: That's part of the committed capacity conversation—how much headroom you want.
[05:29] Kevin: On timeline—if procurement signs end-of-year, when can we be live with a pilot?
[05:35] Priya: Practically, with signed contract + infra inputs, pilot kickoff early to mid-Jan. We suggested Jan 10-12 as options.
[05:43] Sarah: That should work if we get the pricing sheet and SOC2 tonight — procurement will triage fast.
[05:50] Maya: We'll do that. Lucas, anything else from a perf engineering standpoint?
[05:54] Lucas: One more thing: please share a representative traffic trace and a 24–48 hour test deck. Our benchmark will mimic both seq length distribution and burst profile; it helps produce realistic cost projections.
[06:07] Tom: We'll extract and share the traffic.
[06:10] Aisha: On quality gates—what metrics will you use during the pilot to validate no regression?
[06:16] Lucas: We'll run automated evals against your golden prompt set and monitor perplexity / top-k token shifts and SROUGE for reranker outputs. Any deviation beyond agreed thresholds triggers an automatic rollback.
[06:29] Speaker 2: (crosstalk) metric called top-k shifts mentioned.
[06:33] Maya: Great. Let's recap next steps. I'll send the pricing spreadsheet, SOC2 and KMS docs, and the committed tiers. Lucas will run the benchmark once we have the test deck. Tom to share traffic trace and auth matrix. Procurement tasks to Sarah.
[06:52] Sarah: Quick procurement note—we prefer quarterly billing for pilot then convert to annual committed if it meets SLAs.
[06:59] Maya: Fine, we'll add a quarterly pilot billing option in the example SOW.
[07:04] Aisha: Also, small ask: can you include a list of people focused on support SLAs and escalation paths? We want a named on-call if we have incidents during pilot.
[07:14] Priya: Yes, we'll include a support roster and escalation matrix. For Dedicated we can provide a technical account manager if you opt for the premium support add-on.
[07:24] Kevin: Any blockers from Redwood side to start the benchmarks this week?
[07:28] Lucas: We just need the traffic trace and permission to run the synthetic 48-hour job against staging; otherwise we can start.
[07:36] Tom: We'll get that to you by EOD tomorrow.
[07:39] Maya: Excellent. Thanks everyone—we'll email the artifacts and I'll follow up on the calendar invite for the Jan pilot kickoff.
[07:47] Aisha: Thanks.
[07:49] End of meeting.
